facts.statement: The genus Dysalotosaurus was described by Hans Virchow in 1919.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Virchow, 1919

facts.statement: Fossils of Dysalotosaurus have been found in Late Jurassic rocks of the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been found in late Kimmeridgian-age rocks (Late Jurassic) of the Tendaguru Formation of Lindi Region in Tanzania.

facts.statement: Thousands of Dysalotosaurus bones have been recovered from Tanzania since 1909.
facts.quote: Thousands of Dysalotosaurus bones and bone fragments have been recovered from the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania, Africa since 1909

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the many Dysalotosaurus specimens found may represent a single herd killed in a mass death event.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that all of these specimens were part of a herd that was killed in a mass death event.

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus lacked large thumb spikes and had short front limbs with a long tail, adaptations that favored bipedalism over its larger relatives.
facts.quote: It lacked the large thumb spikes found in later iguanodontians, and was more adapted for bipedalism than its larger relatives with its short front limbs and long, counter-balancing tail.

facts.statement: A study of bone cross-sectional geometry confirmed that Dysalotosaurus moved on its hind legs with an erect stance.
facts.quote: A recent comparative study based on bone cross-sectional geometry confirmed its bipedal locomotion with erect stance.

facts.statement: CT scans of the braincase suggest Dysalotosaurus held its head pointing straight forward when not feeding.
facts.quote: Based on CT scans of the braincase, it is believed that Dysalotosaurus held its head dorsally (pointing straight forward) when not feeding.

facts.statement: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Dysalotosaurus to be 2.5 meters long and weigh 80 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2016, Gregory S. Paul estimated Dysalotosaurus' length at 2.5 m, and its weight at 80 kg.

facts.statement: Differences in teeth suggest Dysalotosaurus started as an omnivore but became a fully herbivorous adult.
facts.quote: Differences in dentition as the animals aged also suggest a change from an omnivorous diet early in life to fully herbivorous feeding habits as an adult.

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus likely lived for about twenty years and lived in herds containing individuals of mixed ages.
facts.quote: Dysalotosaurus also appears to have had a life expectancy of roughly twenty years and lived in herds of mixed ages.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dysalotosaurus contain medullary bone tissue, indicating the animal was reproducing.
facts.quote: A tibia (SMNS T3) and a fibula (GPIT/RE/5109) of Dysalotosaurus preserve evidence of medullary bone tissue, which are found in modern birds that are laying eggs in reproduction, and in some other non-avian dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus rex.

facts.statement: A hemivertebra found in a Dysalotosaurus specimen caused scoliosis, marking the first known evidence of this spinal condition in dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The discovery of a hemivertebra (spinal malformation) in another specimen likely caused scoliosis and other pathologic effects on the animal during its life. This malformation occurs in almost every vertebrate clade, though this is the first known evidence of the condition in dinosaurs.

facts.statement: During the Jurassic, the habitat of Dysalotosaurus was a semi-arid coastline of Gondwana featuring tidal flats and lagoons.
facts.quote: During the Jurassic, Tendaguru was part of the semi-arid coastline of Gondwana. Dysalotosaurus fossils were discovered in strata that were deposited in structures characteristic of tidal flats and lagoons.

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus was a medium-sized animal with long hind legs and a tail longer than half its body, which helped it run quickly.
facts.quote: Dysalotosaurus era un animal de tamaño medio, con largas patas traseras y una cola de más de la mitad de su cuerpo que lo ayudaban a correr rápidamente.

facts.statement: The front of Dysalotosaurus' mouth had a horny beak used for browsing, and it possibly had cheek pouches on the sides.
facts.quote: El extremo de su boca presentaba un pico córneo que utilizaba para ramonear, y posiblemente carrillos en los laterales.

facts.statement: In 2003, Maier reported that bones of individuals approximately one-third larger than the Berlin skeleton are known.
facts.quote: Maier en 2003 afirma que también se conocen los huesos de individuos aproximadamente un tercio más grandes que el esqueleto de Berlín.

facts.statement: In 1993, Heinrich, Ruff, and Weishampel estimated the weight of an adult Dysalotosaurus at approximately 70 kilograms.
facts.quote: Heinrich, Ruff y Weishampel en 1993 estimaron el peso de un adulto de D. lettowvorbecki en aproximadamente 70 kilogramos.

facts.statement: In 2011, Hübner calculated the weight of one of the largest known Dysalotosaurus individuals at 116.53 kilograms based on a distal femoral tip.
facts.quote: Hübner en 2011, al examinar la punta femoral distal marcada como MB.R.2144, perteneciente a uno de los individuos más grandes conocidos, calculó el peso del animal en 116,53 kg.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dysalotosaurus were found in Late Upper Jurassic rocks of the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: Sus fósiles se han hallado en rocas de edad de finales del Jurásico Superior de la Formación Tendaguru, Tanzania.

facts.statement: The species Dysalotosaurus was named by Virchow in 1919.
facts.quote: Dysalotosaurus fue nombrado por Virchow en 1919.

facts.statement: The genus Dysalotosaurus was formally described in 1920 by Josef Pompeckja.
facts.quote: El género fue descrito formalmente solo en 1920 por Josef Pompeckia.

facts.statement: Much of the D. lettowvorbecki material, including most articulated skeletons examined by Pompeckja, was destroyed by Allied bombing or disappeared during World War II.
facts.quote: Una gran parte de los huesos de D. lettowvorbecki, incluyendo la mayoría de los esqueletos articulados examinados por Pompeckja fueron destruidos por los bombardeos aliados sobre Alemania durante la Segunda Guerra Mundial o desaparecieron durante la misma.

facts.statement: Of the surviving specimens, only one retains approximately 50% of the skeleton.
facts.quote: Entre los especímenes que han sobrevivido, sólo uno conserva aproximadamente el 50% del esqueleto.

facts.statement: In 1977, Peter Galton argued that the similarities between Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki and Dryosaurus altus were large enough to justify classifying them in the same genus.
facts.quote: Peter Galton en 1977, comparó los fósiles de Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki con los de Dryosaurus altus de Norteamérica. Declaró que las similitudes entre ellos son lo suficientemente grandes como para justificar que no sean clasificados en géneros distintos.

facts.statement: Eventually, Galton considered Dysalotosaurus a junior synonym of Dryosaurus but kept D. lettowvorbecki as a separate species within the genus Dryosaurus.
facts.quote: Eventualmente, Galton consideró a Dysalotosaurus como un sinónimo más moderno de Dryosaurus,, sin embargo, mantuvo a D. lettowvorbecki como una especie separada dentro del género Dryosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2008, Rauhut and López-Arbarello considered that the assignment of Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki to the type of Dryosaurus had not been sufficiently demonstrated.
facts.quote: Rauhut y López-Arbarello en 2008 consideraron que la pertenencia de Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki al tipo de Dryosaurus no se ha demostrado suficientemente.

facts.statement: The name Dysalotosaurus means "hard-to-catch lizard" in Greek and likely refers to the animal's light body.
facts.quote: El nombre significa tanto como "lagarto difícil de atrapar", del griego Δυσάλωτος dysálōto "difícil de atrapar" y σαύρα saur "lagarto" en latín y es probablemente, en alusión al cuerpo ligero del animal.

facts.statement: The species name D. lettowvorbecki honors German officer Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, who served in German East Africa during World War I.
facts.quote: La segunda parte del nombre de la especie, D. lettowvorbecki, honra a Paul von Lettow-Vorbeck, un oficial alemán que sirvió durante la Primera Guerra Mundial en el África Oriental Alemana.

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus is included in the family Dryosauridae, a basal group within Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: Dysalotosaurus se encuentra incluido en la familia Dryosauridae, un grupo basal dentro de Iguanodontia.

facts.statement: In 2011, Barrett included Dysalotosaurus with the genera Valdosaurus and Elrhazosaurus in a clade within Dryosauridae based on similarities in the upper metatarsal bones.
facts.quote: Barrett en 2011 incluye a Dysalotosaurus con los géneros Valdosaurus y Elrhazosaurus en un clado dentro de los Dryosauridae, basándose en las similitudes de los huesos metatarsianos superiores.

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus reached sexual maturity at approximately ten years of age.
facts.quote: Dysalotosaurus era un dinosaurio precoz, que experimentaba su madurez sexual a los diez años de edad

facts.statement: The dinosaur exhibited indeterminate growth with a maximum growth rate comparable to that of a large kangaroo.
facts.quote: poseía un patrón de crecimiento indeterminado, y una tasa de crecimiento máximo comparable al de un canguro grande

facts.statement: Growth accelerated until about 14 years of age, reaching a mass of approximately 60 kilograms.
facts.quote: En los años siguientes, el crecimiento se aceleró, alcanzando una tasa comparable a la de los marsupiales, el crecimiento más rápido duró hasta aproximadamente la edad de 14 años, cuando Dysalotosaurus alcanzaba una masa de aproximadamente 60 kilogramos

facts.statement: No fossil eggs or bones of newborn individuals of Dysalotosaurus are known.
facts.quote: No se conocen fósiles de huevos o huesos de individuos recién nacidos de Dysalotosaurus

facts.statement: In the largest known specimens, neurocentral sutures in the tail were fully closed while others remained open, confirming that growth was not yet complete.
facts.quote: En los especímenes más grandes conocidos de Dysalotosaurus se han cerrado completamente las suturas neurocentrales en la cola, pero no en otros sectores, lo que confirma que incluso en estos el crecimiento aún no ha terminado

facts.statement: CT scans suggest Dysalotosaurus held its mouth inclined upward at an angle of approximately 17 degrees in its resting position.
facts.quote: Sobre esta base, se encontró que en la posición de descanso, Dysalotosaurus sostenía la boca inclinada hacia arriba en un ángulo de aproximadamente 17°

facts.statement: The relatively short cochlea indicates a best hearing range of approximately 3500 Hertz.
facts.quote: El caracol era relativamente corto, de 9,67 milímetros desde la base de 36 milímetros del cráneo, lo que indica que el rango de mejor audición fue de aproximadamente 3500 Hertz

facts.statement: In 2011, researchers discovered bone deformities in Dysalotosaurus were likely caused by a viral infection similar to osteitis deformans or Paget's disease.
facts.quote: En 2011 los paleontólogos Florian Witzmann y Oliver Hampe y sus colaboradores, del Museo de Historia Natural de Berlín, descubrieron que las deformaciones de algunos huesos de Dysalotosaurus fueron probablemente causadas por una infección viral similar a la osteítis deformante o enfermedad de Paget

facts.statement: This represents the oldest known evidence of a viral infection in the scientific record.
facts.quote: Esta es la prueba más antigua de infección viral conocida hasta ahora por la ciencia

facts.statement: The genus Dysalotosaurus was named by Virchow in 1919.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Dysalotosaurus (genus), Virchow 1919

facts.quote: Parent group: Dryosauridae

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus is classified within the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Dysalotosaurus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (152.21 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: New anatomical information and ontogenetic changes were published in 2026 based on the study of an immature individual from the Tendaguru Formation in Tanzania.
facts.quote: Rocchi et al. (2026) provide new information on the anatomy of Dysalotosaurus lettowvorbecki and changes in its skeleton during its ontogeny on the basis of the study of an immature individual from the Tendaguru Formation (Tanzania)
